title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-08-19

ai_review.summary: High‑quality audience tape of a 1970 show with an exceptional acoustic set and stand‑out performances of Lovelight, Good Lovin' and How Long Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording captures a vibrant 1970 concert where the acoustic half shines—Pigpen’s piano, tight vocal harmonies, and barn‑burning versions of Lovelight and How Long Blues—while the electric set delivers a fiery Good Lovin'.  Technical fidelity is surprisingly good for an audience cassette, though occasional rough edges and a slightly out‑of‑tune electric segment are noted.  Overall the show is praised as one of the era’s highlights.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award 4–5 stars, lauding the performance and calling the tape "clean" and "crisp," while a few note tuning issues; weighted toward show quality gives a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners commend Taback’s mic placement, crisp separation and lively sound, though some mention rough edges and occasional out‑of‑tune moments in the electric set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The acoustic set is described as beautiful and tightly arranged, leading into a high‑energy electric half where Good Lovin' and Lovelight provide the emotional peaks; overall pacing is praised despite minor tuning hiccups.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his pedal‑steel wizardry, expressive solos (e.g., New Speedway Boogie) and tasteful lead work on Good Lovin'.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for lively, well‑defined bass that shines thanks to the clean audience mic placement.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s scattershot honky‑tonk piano is highlighted throughout the acoustic set; keyboards add depth but occasional tentative feel is mentioned.
